tips.comment: Jack The Savage likes to settle handy in a race that looks to have decent pace here. He was held last time at Stratford over 2m6 23 days ago but usually runs better than that on sounder ground and when given a patient ride. His mark of 95 is fair to me now given previous wins and places at this level. Tongue strap and cheekpieces stay on, which have brought some place runs before. Trained by Liz Horsfall and ridden by Sean P O'Connor. Win strike rate 6% and place rate of 19%. Every chance today with this better trip and pace setup.
The trainer doesn't run many here, and this one making his handicap debut is worth a small each way in a poor race.

Zubaru has been consistent in similar races and is now well drawn with a strong jockey booking in Callum Shepherd. He’s been racing over tougher tracks and now finds a slightly easier opening at Doncaster. With a strong pace likely, he could be the one finishing best from off the speed at a fair price.
Pick: Zubaru ??' To Win @9.00

It's what I get for waiting, I guess. This was 25-1 earlier, and I thought if it stays soft, it will have decent chances today. Now only 10-1, but I still have to back it. It's down in grade today with a visor replacing cheek pieces.

STIRRUP CUP returns to a lower grade and won on soft ground when last seen at this level. Gets similar conditions today and is only two pounds above last winning mark so is probably going to turn the corner before too long. Not offered too much this season, but is getting slightly closer each time so one to consider.
Drops down 10lb below winning mark. Useful 5lb claiming jockey takes the ride for the first time. Jockey rides well at this course.

The 5yo has 6 wins on turf and loves the slow ground. He went close in a strong class 2 handicap two weeks ago, made the more pleasing as that came on fast ground. He was rated 7lb higher as recently as April, four runs back. He should be a big player in this class 4 handicap on soft ground.

Shajak could well be in the mix. He's a consistent placer in cheekpieces, shaped better than the bare result last time. Proven on similar ground, capable of improvement from easing mark for in-form yard with useful 5 lb claim.

This one looks to be too big a price based on his last run. He finished well from a different parish at Newcastle and is better off at the weights with the winner tonight. He's better on good ground so wouldn't want too much rain.
Dropped in the market, but believe still has every chance to get in the placings. Outstayed last time out, and drop back in trip seems the one.
Maybe this one can have a change of luck tonight for his in form yard. The jockey is in a rich vein of form too.
Won a couple of handicaps at Southwell and Musselburgh and still in form judging on a 4th place last time out in a hot race.

I have done quite well over the last couple of years in these Racing League meetings (bet a lot on Wales & the West with Saffie rides), but I think it will be tougher this year and today could be even harder with this soft/heavy going. Minhad, I believe, is making his handicap debut today, and it was made known after his win at Newmarket (good/firm) that he really needs/prefers soft going, and that's what he gets today in this class 4 race. He was a bit out of his depth in a Group 2 at Ascot last time out and, in my opinion, has received a quite generous opening mark, so really has no excuses. But these races are very competitive, so let's see.

Trained by James Ferguson and ridden by Richard Kingscote, this 4-year-old Masar gelding has already shown he handles Yarmouth, having claimed victory over 10f last season. He ran a solid second over 12f at Salisbury just 12 days ago, beaten by only half a length and conceding weight, suggesting he's primed to go one better today. With the same conditions in his favor and no penalty for that recent run, he looks one to watch.

Sword Of Wessex has his first outing after a gelding operation which may produce better form. Lightly raced, he is very well bred being by Europe's current leading sire of the season Wootton Bassett out of a Galileo mare. The granddam produced Derby winner Pour Moi. The stable's penultimate runner was a winner. Harry Davies, whose penultimate ride was a winner, takes over in the saddle.
Has the advantage of being the only C&D winner in this field. Has struggled for consistency since the last win at Newcastle last July but should welcome the dropped mark this time out.

I've been following this horse when it was trained by Varian. Now with Osborne and has Saffie riding tonight. It has to overcome a wide draw, but this horse finished close to Ombudsman and looks capable of winning a race like this.
This one looks a great price to me. His run last time can be ignored as he was hampered. He's won over course and distance, and his yard looks to be hitting form.

Flying Fletcher appears to be returning to form. He carried a lot of weight (9 stone 12 pounds) when fifth of 11 in a Class 4 at Doncaster, keeping on late and not beaten far. Runs off a rating one pound lower now but bottom weight in this Class 3 contest carrying 8 stone 6 pounds this evening. Soft ground might even be to his liking also. Cam Hardie rides this 4yo Muharrar grey for Richard Fahey. Mostly tried on AW, now 2 lbs below last winning mark.

King of Bears, a 3-year-old bay gelding, was given a high handicap mark for his 3-year-old season. He changed stables from Paul Cole to George Scott on 24-6-2025. Slowly coming down the handicap and therefore becoming a betting proposition. Nice each way price here.

Brooklyn Nine Nine was winning for the third time in his career when taking a Class 5 handicap at Hamilton last month. That was off 77, and although up 4 lbs, his previous winning mark was 82, so he can still be competitive and looks a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.

A beaten favourite over the extended 5 furlongs at Chester last time out and beaten a short head there over this 5 furlong trip in the race subsequent to that. His last win came off this mark of 81 over this trip at Windsor in August 2024.
Two wins and two seconds from six career starts suggests each way possibilities and is proven on the soft going encountered today. Has also only once been out of the places at today's distance.

Not clicked in two starts for this yard in 2025, though debut at Sandown was better than it looked. Now just 1 above last winning mark, which was in similar conditions to today. Might get an easy time in front and looks like a potential improver who's worth an each-way go at 25/1 IMO.
Turned round quickly after finishing third over this trip at Windsor on Monday. Remains on the same mark and the first time blinkers are of interest.

EXPRESS TRAIN has won a race at 6f. A winner on his latest outing over 6f at Leicester earlier this month, winning easily. Course, distance, and going should suit. Seems well treated and could well be able to go in again and win this race.

Thunder Blue is a 4-year-old gelding trained by Jamie Osborne. His best recent run came at Newcastle some six starts back when finishing 2/14 behind the extremely progressive Heathcliff (80), who has won again two starts later at Kempton, making it 4/13 wins and has risen from a mark of 69 to 92, some 23lb and posted a personal best RPR of 98 and received 8lb from Thunder Blue in a class 3 contest. Thunder Blue has generally been campaigning over 7f but drops to 6f today for a trainer in Jamie Osborne, who has an excellent recent record with 6f handicap sprinters in class 4-6 handicaps over 6f, winning with 15 of his last 78 runners since 2024, showing a healthy LSP of £74.50. Osborne has won with 3 of his last 4 runners meeting this criteria: Amazing Journey 5-2, Em Four 4-1, and Many A Star 12-1. So it's highly likely that Thunder Blue is primed and ready for a tilt at this valuable class 4 prize under Saffie Osborne.

Tiger Tulip has found some excellent form, winning a 6-runner Class 4 handicap at Windsor in May. She followed up in a 17-runner Newbury handicap last month, winning by 2 lengths. She is up 9 lbs here but looks sure to go well again and looks like a good each-way bet with 4 places on offer.
Finley Marsh is on board this Lingfield winner who is yet to go over soft ground. He hasn't found good to firm to his taste, so soft may be a hit.

Backing Mostawaa, the battle-hardened 9-year-old Poet's Voice gelding trained by Heather Main, in tomorrow’s Racing League Handicap (1m3y, Class 4). He arrives in fine fettle, having finished a close 3rd of 14 at Carlisle in late June??'leading until the final furlong and edged out only in the dying strides??'showing he remains competitive.
A proven front-runner, Mostawaa often dictates terms early before tiring late, and tomorrow's soft ground looks ideal to help him sustain his gallop. His Carlisle effort on similar going confirms his liking for slower turf. With a rating of 75 and recurring consistency??'always in the mix according to his season and lifetime records??'he's a strong each-way contender.
In this 14-runner race, expect him to break smartly, set a decent tempo, and aim to dominate again, only to be caught late by those with stamina. Priced around 11/1, he offers both form and pace-play appeal.

Mount King looks a value bet today, bringing solid handicap form and a competitive mark of 72 into a race lacking standout improvers. He ran better than the result suggests when fourth at Pontefract, not getting a clear run and finishing with purpose, indicating there's still more to come. David Allen takes the ride for the in-form Easterby yard, and with the ground and trip both ideal, he could prove a strong finisher in a race that should be run to suit. An underrated contender capable of getting his head in front.

His better form has come on the AW where he has done most of his running of late, but he is too well handicapped to ignore here considering he is 10lb lower than when 7th in a Class 2 handicap at Sandown, just over a year ago. A race he would have won comfortably with 10lb less on his back. This is very much an easier race and he has been knocking on the door recently.

BAJAN BANDIT took a step forward on the second run for new connections last time out and has form on soft ground for the previous stable. So, he might be able to get close from a big price here. Usual caveats with this being a Racing League meeting, which have proved notoriously difficult puzzles in the past.

I was going to leave this race. Then, as the price is drifting, I was going to tip Saffie's ride (who really is now a decent value each way bet). But I'm not going to pick all her rides, and with this going today, there are surely going to be a few big price winners. This team, as a rule, do quite poorly, so I'm hoping they do better this year. 8-year-old Hartswood was in really decent form through the winter on the all-weather and finished off with another win on turf in March at Donny. Returned for what looked like a freshen-up race last month, and if carrying on from that winter form, could at least nick a place at a huge 40-1. (Can cope with going.)

Preference here goes to the John Butler runner, Zain Blue. Looked to be heading back in the right direction when finishing four out of twelve at York over an extended 1m2f at big odds when last seen. Midfield runner that looks well drawn in stall five to find a good position. Acts well on slower ground and an easing mark can only heighten his chances. Well handicapped over his previous mile efforts, so you can build a case he may come on over likable conditions over this trip. Goes off an attractive weight carry that could bring him into contention.
Has some very nice form in handicap races. Was 3rd last time out at Windsor and could still be well handicapped and build on that run.

Premier is in stall 8, which is not ideal for him as he likes to be a prominent racer. But with a decent pace likely, he may still get cover and slot in. He has been consistent lately, finishing third on his last two starts, including a solid run at Sandown 41 days ago off this same mark of 71, which still looks very fair. He has placed twice at this trip and goes fine on this ground, while his win last season at Bath shows he knows how to dig in and battle on. Trained by Warren Greatrex and ridden by Charles Bishop. Win strike rate 14% and place rate 43%. On my shortlist again here.
Meleri is in consistent form, proven over 12f, and recently won off just 3lb lower; handles the ground, experienced at this level, and should go close if building on recent efforts.
Wasn't beaten far on debut when finishing third over C&D at the end of last month despite a slow start. Cost 85,000 guineas as a yearling. Should progress further today. Should be thereabouts. NAP

Calendar Girl is a 2yo filly trained by Owen Burrows (only runner today and is 4/7 wins of late). She is ridden by Jim Crowley, who, when combining with Burrows, has 107/438 wins, showing a healthy LSP of £112.54. Owners Kennet Valley Syndicates (Thoroughbreds) II have had one horse, Equality (Charles Hills), with 6/30 wins and won a Group 1 at Sandown in July '23. Calendar Girl is probably above average and is a second foal related to Gutsy Girl, who won as a 2yo for JP O'Brien, a top yard like Burrows' yard. Very appealing at 9-1.

Fan Me is in stall 4, which is fine tactically, though she will need to break sharper than last time, especially with a strong pace. She was well beaten on debut at Newmarket just 12 days ago and now steps into a handicap off 72, which is hard to assess but not overly harsh given her pedigree. She is by Too Darn Hot out of a Group-placed Sea The Stars mare and is a half-sister to winners, including Ready To Venture. Trainer William Haggas is excellent at improving horses second time out. Still a bit raw but could outrun her odds today. Small each way stakes at 22/1.

Won a seller by a neck on penultimate start, but was value for so much more than the winning margin suggests. Then bettered that form when runner-up in a decent maiden last time. Opening mark of 76 on handicap debut today probably underestimates him.

Cheshire Belle is in stall 4, which is handy and gives her every chance to settle early in behind the leaders with a fair pace on. She has yet to show much in three starts, including finishing sixth of seven last time out at Windsor 38 days ago, but she now makes her handicap debut off a mark of 64, which is very workable based on her staying pedigree. She is by Shaman out of a Cape Cross mare and should improve over further. With David Egan onboard, he is an eye-catcher, and trainer Hugo Palmer is doing very well. Could run better today and surprise.
Flushing Meadows looks about the best bet on the card at Leopardstown. One of the better juveniles from Aidan O'Brien's yard. Defeat is out of the question according to staff we know from Ballydoyle.

This has the look of a strong maiden, but Montreal is an exciting prospect for Ballydoyle. Sea The Stars colt out of an Elusive Quality mare, half-brother to Group 2 winner. Early signs are that this January colt is a bit useful. Will know more than some of the debutants starting racecourse career in August and over 1 mile. Lots of potential here and market looks keen. Ryan Moore (SR 32%) rides for Aidan O'Brien.

Composing - top connections involved here. Not sure what the tactics will be, but should be up on speed if not leading in a small field. Should improve again, showing class in last run. Well bred by Wootton Bassett, and both trainer and jockey have fine records here, both running over 20%. They have teamed up to win the last 3 runnings of this race.
Close behind Beauty and Lady Iman in a group 2 race last time out. Form like that suggests she has enough in her to win today. Step up in trip should help the horse here.

TEQUILA TALKIN was returning from a mammoth break of 609 days when finishing 3rd of 18 runners in June. She finished ahead two of her market rivals, Sophia Rose and Hillhead Runner, that day. She is bound to have improved for that experience and looks the best horse in the race. Local trainer, Nolan, has a great record at Wexford. Still unexposed after only two runs, her ceiling could be anywhere. Confident win bet.
Promising horse with lots of potential. Interesting in this field, was staying on last time out and should run into a place.

Finished 3rd on her hurdles debut over 17f at Tipperary in mid May despite a rather mixed round of jumping. Made mistakes last time at Punchestown when seemingly struggling with the pace over the two mile trip. There should be more to come at some stage and perhaps this step up in distance will help and a better round of jumping could see her feature.

Not only do I like the name, but I also loved the way she ran. Absolute Bliss is a newcomer to hurdles and should settle comfortably behind the pace. She was well held in a bumper here 57 days ago after not getting a clear run but showed me enough to say she could improve over hurdles and stepping up in trip. Off a short break and now under the care of Paul Tobin with jockey D J O'Keeffe aboard. Current mark OR of 109 looks fair for a first-time hurdler, and she may need the run but could surprise at big odds here at 40/1. Each way chance if she settles well today.
Improved form lately and keeps on getting better. Travelled well last time out in a 12-runner field. Big chances to run well here.

Gets a swing in the weights, reopposing a narrow defeat to Rose Boum, and followed that effort up with a respectable run to subsequent winner Crowsatedappletart, who won yesterday. Should be winning one soon.
Knockraha Eagle steps up to twenty furlongs after staying on over shorter last time out and must have a competitive chance in this contest if building upon that.

Been a while since FEAST showed good levels of form in bumpers but he does have a modicum of talent and should be spot on after his recent Downpatrick run following a long break. Each way chances in a very poor race.

Dancing Teapot is in stall 2, which is ideal for her prominent run style and should allow her to get a smooth early position in what looks like a fairly even pace setup. She ran below par last time at Ascot 34 days ago when hampered, so we can excuse that run. Her mark of 84 is still very reasonable based on her earlier runs, including a tidy win two starts back. She handles this ground well, and the tongue strap, which brought success, returns, and cheekpieces are added this time round. Trained by Joseph O'Brien and ridden by Dylan McMonagle. Win strike rate 33% and place rate 50% makes her a win chance here.

Menas Miracle showed little in 4 maiden hurdles, but she looked immediately well handicapped at Tramore in May when a clear 2nd behind the favourite in a 2m5f handicap. That trip seemed to stretch her stamina, but dropped back to 2m2f, she won here at Wexford by 4 lengths earlier this month. She is 10lbs higher here, but this is only her 7th start, so she can go well again and looks like a good EW bet with 4 places on offer.
Looked a big threat last time out before weakening. If able to build on that, should kick on and get a win here. Big player.
Menas Miracle is in fine form but may struggle with a hike at the weights and QUINN THE ESKIMO is taken to return to winning ways dropped back in trip.
Yet to win from 7 starts over hurdles but did finish a good 3rd of 14 on penultimate outing in January. Holds an each-way chance if in that same form on first start since February.

Already with an introduction at distance, Spinning Around can come on for that run and show more. The well-bred Australia filly was soundly beaten but not given a hard time once her chance had gone. She's taken to put that experience to good use in this contest.

Well backed late into favouritism at Roscommon over three miles last time. Under a well judged ride from today's jockey Conor Stone-Walsh, Small Town Hero stayed on to win with what looked a little in hand on first run for new stable of Ian Donoghue. Only up 4lbs, receiving weight from the majority of rivals, makes a fair bet at 5-1 to go in again.
No comment made

I think at this trip it's worth having a little skin in the game with James Barcoe's 7 year old Gelding GLAOINN AN AIRGEAD who ran a career best 9 days ago at Downpatrick (22f Good) keeping on when finishing 6th so the intrigue has me interested as to wether the step up in trip is what this lad wants. This Son of RAJJ gets another 7lb claimer on top this time in the shape of the talented Harry Sexton who has rattled the frame 3 times this past fortnight (27.27% place strike rate) with trainer hitting a 33.33% place strike rate over the same time frame. I wouldn't be racing down to the bookies & putting the Mortgage on the line but a casual stroll and a few bits of loose change wouldn't hurt & with 25/1 odds on offer - why not.

Tackletommywoowooo showed a bit of form when raced in Britain in a few bumpers that showed there was a small race to be had with him. At Listowel in May, he was a good second over 3m before racing poorly and falling at the last fence at Kilbeggan. I'm willing to bet there is some progress left in him and he can bounce back.
Had been in good form over hurdles before disappointing twice over the bigger obstacles. Can get back to winning ways now returning to hurdles.

40/1 is way too big a price for me to ignore for Chris Timmons 6 year old Mare ROYAL CAVE who I genuinely believe has THREE valid excuses for her previous runs: 1] The All weather Run at Dundalk can clearly be chalked off. 2] we had a 131 day break to overcome at Kilbeggan & 3] the Yielding/Soft Ground would have done this Daughter of COURT CAVE no favours. Which now brings us to two very good runs a decent 2nd at Kilbeggan over this trip was turn followed by a very good run at Fairyhouse which saw this charge denied at the last when it looked like she would make all. That was off a mark of 92 which she returns to today under the tutelage of Top Pro Jordan Gainford who has a 28.42% place strike rate here the past 5 years. Trainer has a 40% place strike rate the past fortnight. You would like to think that this Mare has a race of this nature in her locker & back down to a competitive mark I think it would be unwise to totally write her off as she returns back to favourable conditions.
The nap goes to TELAS KERA who is quite smartly bred for the flat and wouldn't need to be anything brilliant to win a bumper as weak as this.

I am throwing one in at a big price here because of connections. The yard does not run many but does tend to do well with what they run at Wexford, and this newcomer will not have to be special to land this on debut.
Showed some promise on debut earlier this month at Tipperary but still only finished 8th of 16. Should be better than that, and any improvement gives an each-way chance.

Curious Bride is an 8-year-old mare trained by Eamonn O'Connell. She is a three-time winner on the flat off marks of 64-65-69 over distances varying between 12-17f, twice under Colin Keane and the latter win at Clonmel under a 2lb conditional. She has won on todays soft to heavy over hurdles. Curious Bride showed signs of a revival last time out at Tramore, beaten 3/4l, posting an RPR of 71 under Killian Leonard (no claim). She takes her chance today under the promising 10lb apprentice Conor Cusack who has recently won two flat races for Henry De Bromhead, putting his claim to good use. Curious Bride runs today off a mark of 61 with the apprentice on board, a mark below her last three wins, and can figure if building on her latest effort.
The Truant beat Makiah at Navan by 1 1/2 lengths back in April. He has form on soft ground and could bounce back in a wide-open race. Each way hopeful.
